Date : 13/02/2020
Per Court :

The applicant is seeking bail in anticipation of his arrest in connection with Crime
No. 17/2019, registered with Vazirabad Police Station, Nanded, for the offences
punishable under Section 188, 272, 273, 328 of the Indian Penal Code and under
Section 59 of the Food, Safety and Standards Act, 2006.
2.  The applicant is stated to have been found in possession of scented tobacco, Ghutka, Panmasala etc. which was seized.
Samples were drawn.
F.I.R. was lodged by an officer under the Food and Safety Act.
The crime was registered for the aforementioned sections.

3. The learned advocate for the applicant submits that since there are no allegations about the substance having been administered 910 aba 1501 19.odt to anybody, the Provisions of Section 328 of the Indian Penal Code would not be attracted.
The rest of the offences being bailable, the muddemal having been already seized, custodial interrogation of the applicant is not necessary.
He is ready to abide by all the terms and conditions and may be granted bail.

sentences.text: The learned A.P.P. opposes the application.
He submits that there is a genuine dispute as to the applicability of Section 328 of the Indian Penal Code.
The issue can only be decided during full fledged trial.
Huge quantity of Ghutkha and other material has been recovered.
This is not a first instance, the applicant is habituated in this activity.
Already thrice he has been involved in similar kind of offences and still has involved in this offence.
There is every room to believe that he would repeat the crime.
The application may be rejected.
5. Indeed there are several decisions touching applicability of Section 328 of the Indian Penal Code to a fact situation in the matter in hand which can only be decided at a full fledged trial.
The fact remains that the stock has already been seized.
It is not the allegation that the applicant had administered the substance to anybody.
Except Section 328 of the Indian Penal Code the rest of the offences are bailable.

6. True it is that the applicant seems to be indulging in similar kind of offences and therefore,
necessary precaution will have to be taken to obviate his getting involved in any such activity at least hereafter.
7.
In the facts and circumstances, the application deserves to be allowed.
The application is allowed.

In the event of arrest of applicant he shall be released on bail on his executing personal recognizance for an amount of Rs. 25,000/- and furnishing a solvent surety in the like amount subject to following conditions :
(a) He shall attend the concerned police station on first Monday of every month between 9 a.m. and 11 a.m., till conclusion of the trial.
(b) His involvement in an offence of similar kind hereafter shall result in automatic cancellation of his bail.
(c) He shall not tamper the evidence or influence the witnesses.
